The packet's p=0.7562792633170974, k=8 bound is 2.9563438658645618, an idealized ceiling rather than a measured gain. Device setup, host generation, validation, cleanup, and the untimed 6.7187% constrain end-to-end gains. GPU telemetry exists, but GPU stage times are unavailable and this profile does not establish held-out workload performance. Eight logical shards are a prospective scheduling choice, not eight GPUs. Keep sealed hardware_cost_basis baseline_gpus=1 and method_gpus=2 unchanged despite the candidate's one-GPU requirement; record actual participation separately and use the sealed accounting basis without silently substituting one GPU. Predictions at 300, 600 and 1200 gpu_s are conditional: full fixed workload completion and unrounded Average reserve strictly greater than 1 are required; completion and pass probabilities remain unmeasured.

risks: Single-GPU pricing may already saturate compute or memory resources. Extra streams, kernel launches, RNG states, buffers, transfers, scheduling and merge may erase predicted gains or increase memory pressure; the idealized eight-way bound is not evidence of available hardware concurrency.

The profile is short, only 93.2813% timed by listed stages, and includes allocation and RNG within the compute fraction. Extrapolation to the fixed held-out workload is uncertain; no measured completion or acceptance probabilities support the budget predictions.

Matched global cuRAND streams and host paired-seed support do not yet exist. Scheduling-dependent subsequences, duplicate or omitted paths, or different random-number consumption break scientific pairing even if both arms pass.

Float accumulation order and shard merging can change unrounded Average reserve near the strict >1 boundary. Preserve global ordering and arithmetic structure where possible; binary acceptance has zero tolerance, while no continuous-reserve equivalence margin is supplied.
Exact environment versions and GPU model are unavailable. Stream or environment mismatch invalidates evaluation; the development anchor is insufficient to establish held-out equivalence.

Keep this basis unchanged and disclose actual utilization; do not conflate wall-time speedup with equal-gpu_s budget performance.
